name: kalshi-horizon-5m-jev
description: The five-minute forecast asked of a decisions model: the derived tools that do the arithmetic, and three typed questions - a distribution over cent moves, the half width of the market to post, and the paper book's order - in place of a written answer. TypeSafe's Jev answers in under a second for about two thousandths of a cent a window. The box also offers ask_opus, ask_sonnet and ask_gpt5_mini, which put the same state to a chat model; this seed does not use them, because each one costs real money on every window.
context:
You forecast the short-term path of a Kalshi sports contract while the match is being played.

You are not asked who wins. You are asked where this contract's mid price will be in five minutes, which is a narrower and more answerable question.

What moves a price on this horizon:
- the game state changing: a goal, a red card, a period ending
- time simply passing, which decays any "will happen" contract toward no, faster as the clock runs down
- the book being thin, so a single order moves the mid and it drifts back
- the market absorbing a goal that happened two or three minutes ago

Most five-minute windows do not move. A quiet book at a stable score with nothing scheduled to happen stays where it is, and saying so is the right answer. A contract near 1c or 99c has almost nowhere to go. A contract in the middle with the score level and the clock past 75' can jump several cents on one event and otherwise sits still.

steps.name: predict

move.instructions: How many cents the contract's mid price moves over the next five minutes, from the book shown now. Positive is up. A quiet book at a settled score usually stays within half a cent.
criteria: unchanged, within half a cent either way

width.instructions: The half width, in cents, of the two-sided market you post on this contract: bid at (the move you just named - this) and offered at (that move + this). This is a choice, not a by-product of how unsure you are. The path will travel through a width that is too narrow and take BOTH your sides, at prices the market has already left behind - every one of those fills is adversely selected and pays a maker fee on top. A width nobody reaches never trades and costs exactly nothing, which is what standing aside scores. Over this question set the five-minute path reaches a median of two and a half cents from the mid and a tenth of windows reach seventeen, so a one-cent market is run over on both sides in almost half of them. Read the base rate's p50 and p90 and quote outside the range you expect the path to cover.

action.instructions: What the paper book should do with this contract now, given the move you expect against a round trip of two to three cents in spread and taker fees.

criteria.open_long: buy YES at the ask: the mid rises by more than the round trip
criteria.open_short: buy NO at one minus the bid: the mid falls by more than the round trip
criteria.close: take an open position off at the touch
criteria.hold: do nothing: no edge worth the spread and the fee

size.instructions: How much of the book's equity to put in this contract if opening. Nothing when holding or closing; the cap is a tenth.

driver.value: the expectation of the move distribution

falsifier.value: a print outside the quoted band before five minutes are up
